RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

A panel’s demographic makeup is not evidence of bias; hiring committees usually reflect available administrative roles, and education has high female representation. Citing the panel's gender without hard proof will damage your professional reputation and appear defensive. 

While unconscious bias cannot be entirely ruled out in any recruitment, principal appointments heavily weigh interview performance, strategic vision, references, and institutional fit, not just credentials on paper. 

Do not mention the panel’s gender. Instead, follow up professionally on your request for the written explanation. If you later uncover procedural irregularities or scoring discrepancies that contradict the job criteria, address those objective facts through formal channels.
